inputs.prompt: Requested framing: Close-up. Edit the reference photograph into a new camera shot of the SAME scene. Preserve the exact same person and facial identity, hair, outfit, bag, object design, materials, lighting and set architecture from the reference. Change camera position and framing as requested; do not simply repeat the reference composition. TIGHT FACE CLOSE-UP: the reference woman with the exact same rounded face, lowered eyes, light chestnut chin-length bob with soft waves curling outward at the ends and right side part, mustard yellow canvas coat with metal buttons, shoulder tabs and flap chest pockets, rich teal cable-knit scarf. Her face fills the portrait frame, cropped just above the head and below the teal scarf. Keep her head tilted and eyes lowered exactly as in the reference, her facial proportions, skin texture and age unchanged. Keep hair colour, side part, soft waves and outward-curled ends unchanged. Show the teal knit scarf and mustard coat collar at the bottom edge. Keep the greenhouse window grid softly blurred. No hands or compass in frame, no eye contact, no added forehead or eye wrinkles. This is a camera push-in, NOT a restyling of her hair or face. Preserve every large wave clump and the loose outward-fanning curls at jaw level on BOTH sides, exactly as in the reference. Leave the whole bob outline visible, including the loose tips that curl OUTWARD away from the cheeks; do not tuck the lower ends inward against the ears or neck. Keep the original forehead, brow spacing, nose, closed relaxed lips and rounded face proportions without lengthening or slimming. Keep the same bulky rolled cable-knit loop with clearly twisted cables under her chin. Frame the whole head and just the upper scarf; no chest, hands, object, inset image or strip along bottom.. Keep only elements visible in this framing; do not force a face into a detail or rear view.
